title: Materials & shading
notes: These are actual materials in our Unreal project: a smooth response, brush-shaped bands, and a chosen palette. We will build from small calculations to these artistic choices. The appearance changes even when the underlying mesh stays a sphere.

title: Agenda · 4:30–7:00 PM
notes: We start with a small shader example before Ned joins at five. His thirty-minute block includes questions. Water then leads directly into a twenty-minute investigation. title: Change a material instance
notes: The material instance inherits its graph and defaults from the parent. Tick the box beside Tint before editing the color. If nothing changes, check the material assigned to the mesh and the override checkbox. For the starting state, restore Tint to 0.20, 0.80, 0.45. Ordinary scalar and vector parameters change values. Static switches are a separate type of control that select compiled variants. Scalar and vector overrides change values within the parent material. Static switches select compiled variants, so toggling them can trigger compilation.

title: Color operations
notes: These are familiar image-editing operations expressed as material math. Multiplication is component-wise. Lerp blends toward a chosen value; adding a positive color cannot darken the input. Values used for lighting and emissive effects may exceed one, so clamping every result is not a general rule.

title: Advanced: Gerstner motion
notes: Gerstner is an optional advanced extension. It is useful when crest shape and silhouette matter. Several waves can be combined with different directions, wavelengths, amplitudes, and phases. Keep steepness within a valid range to avoid loops; normals must agree with the displaced surface, and mesh density must support the shortest wave. The GPU Gems chapter explains these equations. Sea of Thieves uses a broader production ocean approach; its paper is not the source code for this Gerstner study.

title: Color building blocks
notes: Reference page; no need to teach every row during the lecture. Multiply / Add: Multiplication is component-wise. A scalar scales every component. Multiplying by white preserves RGB; by black removes it. Mix / Lerp: Alpha 0 returns A; 1 returns B. Values outside 0..1 extrapolate. A color Alpha blends channels independently. Clamp / Saturate: Clamping is not normalization or remapping: values outside the range collapse to the endpoints.

title: Masks and repeating values
notes: Reference page; no need to teach every row during the lecture. Step: Result is 0 when x < edge and 1 otherwise. UE Step uses X for the value and Y for the edge; the code arguments put the edge first. Smoothstep: Keep Min < Max. This softens a value transition; it does not blur a texture or guarantee anti-aliasing. Fract / Frac: Result is x − floor(x), also for negative x. Explicit Frac creates derivative discontinuities; texture wrapping usually handles repeating UVs better.

title: Coordinates and texture data
notes: Reference page; no need to teach every row during the lecture. Time + UV offset: UV speed is repeats per second. Use a float2/vector with two meaningful channels. Mesh positions do not change. Remap a signed field: A sampled .5 becomes zero offset. Import data textures with sRGB OFF. Components / Append: RGBA and XYZW name the same component positions. Appending does not normalize a direction.

title: Lighting building blocks
notes: Reference page; no need to teach every row during the lecture. Normalize + Dot: Use nonzero vectors in the same space. L points toward the light. Dot of unit vectors ranges from -1 to 1 before clamping. Power + view rim: Normalize N and V first. Higher positive power narrows the rim. This artistic mask alone is not a complete Fresnel reflectance model. UE Fresnel adds its own BaseReflectFractionIn parameter and expects a world-space normal. Floor + bands: x is clamped 0..1 and n is an integer ≥2. The Min keeps x=1 at the final level rather than making an extra band.

title: Motion and shader stages
notes: Reference page; no need to teach every row during the lecture. Sine / Cosine: Code sin/cos use radians. UE Sine/Cosine default Period is 1: an input of 1 completes a cycle. Alternatively divide radians by 2π and keep Period 1. Vertex displacement: The GLSL example assumes a local +Z plane. UE WPO uses world units (normally cm), needs enough vertices, and does not automatically update collision. Vertex displacement also needs matching shading normals. DDX / DDY / Fwidth: These are screen derivatives, not an analytic object-space slope. Use in the pixel stage. Discontinuous control flow or values can make them unreliable.

title: DepthFade at an intersection
notes: DepthFade softens the intersection between this translucent plane and the opaque rock. The FadeDistance input uses world units. The Opacity input stays at 0.75, and FadeMix selects the faded result. This is an opacity treatment; it does not make waves or generate foam.

title: Mesh UVs and world projection
notes: Both cubes use the same Epic brick texture. Their initial repeat sizes differ. The left samples mesh UVs. The right calls Epic’s WorldAlignedTexture function and sets repeat size in world units. Move the right cube to see the surface slide through the stationary pattern. That behavior is useful on static surfaces and can be distracting on moving objects.

title: Single Layer Water
notes: Unreal’s SingleLayerWater shading model uses a dedicated pass to show water transmission and scattering while the material uses Opaque or Masked blending. The separate water output supplies volume properties. Here only absorption scale changes. Look at the submerged rock. These settings describe shading, not wave generation.
